rank.method: [RFP] nonsingular 34x34 minor (rows above) certified by ||I - Y*A||_inf = 2.397e-13 < 1 with rounding + IV-radius bound; rank <= 34 is trivial (34 columns). FULLY RIGOROUS.

self_stress.method_dim: [RFP+EXACT] dim ker(A^T) = 38 - rank(A) = 38 - 34 = 4, rank certified above. FULLY RIGOROUS.
self_stress.method_support: [RFP] row k lies in the support of some self-stress iff rank(A_{-k}) = 34; each listed support row has a certified nonsingular 34-minor among the other 37 rows. The 18 NON-support rows are [NUM] only (rank(A_{-k}) = 33 is a rank-deficiency claim).

consequences: no nonzero nonnegative self-stress on the 38 rows (Gordan: sum_k y_k grad g_k = 0 with y >= 0, y != 0 would give 0 = sum_k y_k (grad g_k . y) > 0)
cone{grad g_k} is POINTED (all 38 generators lie in the open halfspace {w . y > 0})
the multiplier polytope {lambda >= 0 : A^T lambda = e_s} is BOUNDED
farkas_no_nonneg_selfstress.method: [IV] LP-found direction rationalised at denominator 1e9; all 38 products grad g_k . y verified > 0 in mpmath.iv at dps 60 over the degenerate point box at z-hat. min_k lower bound = 0.229700. FULLY RIGOROUS.

lambda_star.method: [EXACT+IV] Chebyshev LP (max t s.t. lambda >= t, A^T lambda = e_s) in float64; the 4 rows outside A22's invertible subsystem S frozen at rationalised LP values; the 34 S-rows re-solved at mpmath dps 90 and rationalised at denominator 1e45.  ||A^T lambda* - e_s||_1 then bounded in mpmath.iv (dps 60) at z-hat: 9.680e-45.

task2.method: [NUM] dof = 34 - rank(A_M) from float64 SVD with threshold 1e-9; the spectral gap is recorded per stratum (sv_min_kept vs sv_max_dropped).  dof = 0 ("empty") entries are additionally [RFP]-CERTIFIED for k <= 3 by a nonsingular 34-row minor.  dof > 0 claims are rank-deficiency claims and are [NUM] only.

k1_dof1_summary.identity_note: e_s.v = sum_{b in B} lambda*_b (grad g_b . v) must hold for every retained-kernel v; the residual is a consistency check on lambda*.

vertex_enumeration_cross_check.note: three independent enumerations of the 4-dim multiplier polytope; the C(38,4) sweep can in principle miss a degenerate vertex whose every 4-subset is singular, so it is cross-checked against qhull and 4000 random-objective LPs.

task3.exact_excludability_method: [EXACT combinatorics on the vertex set] a break set B fails to kill the cone iff B avoids the support of some vertex, i.e. iff B is a subset of some Z(v). Enumerating all subsets of the 16 maximal Z(v) gives the exact count of surviving break sets at every size. Uses the retained rows ONLY -- gained contacts are not in the menu.

rows_by_family.note: every surviving break set is drawn from these rows alone; breaking ANY row outside this list already kills the cone.

task3.method_a: [NUM->verified] the multiplier polytope P = {lambda>=0 : A^T lambda = e_s} is bounded (Task 1b) and its affine hull is lambda* + ker(A^T), dim 4. All C(38,4) = 73815 4-subsets solved for the tight vertex; feasible ones deduped. Min support of a vertex = min support over all of P (the minimal-support face contains a vertex). Vertex arithmetic is float64; the extremal vertices are re-verified below in mpmath.
task3.method_b: [IV] for each |B| = 7 the LP  max t s.t. grad g_m . y >= t (m in M), e_s . y = y[33] = -1, |y| <= 50  is solved; y is rationalised at denominator 1e9 and every grad g_m . y is verified > 0 in mpmath.iv at dps 60.  Then lambda >= 0 with A_M^T lambda = e_s would give 0 > e_s.y = sum lambda_m (grad g_m . y) >= 0.  FULLY RIGOROUS per set.

lipschitz_derivation: corner q_i = c_i + R(theta_i) h,  |h| = sqrt(2)/2 = 1/sqrt(2).
|dq_i| <= |dc_i|_2 + |dtheta_i| * |h| <= sqrt(2) R + R/sqrt(2) = (3/sqrt2) R ~ 2.12132 R   for ||dz||_inf <= R.
square i as a set moves at most (3/sqrt2) R in Hausdorff distance (a square is the convex hull of its 4 corners).
the Euclidean separation dist(K_i, K_j) is 1-Lipschitz in the Hausdorff perturbation of each body, so it changes by at most L_pair * R with L_pair = 2*(3/sqrt2) = 3*sqrt(2) ~ 4.24264.
the reported pair gap is the SAT max-over-edge-normals value, which is a LOWER bound on dist and is 0 exactly at contact -- so using it in the screen is conservative.
wall rows: x=0 / y=0 gap changes by <= (3/sqrt2) R ~ 2.12132 R; x=s / y=s also carry ds, so <= (1 + 3/sqrt2) R ~ 3.12132 R.
NOTE the brief's suggested 2*sqrt(2) R = 2.82843 R sits between the per-square constant 2.12132 and the pair constant 4.24264; the larger (conservative) constants are used here.
task4.noncontact_pair_gaps_method: [IV] SAT separation (max over the 8 edge-normal axes) enclosed in mpmath.iv at dps 60 over the degenerate point box at z-hat.
task4.candidate_definition: BOTH screens are NECESSARY conditions for the pair/row to reach contact within travel R, so the sound candidate set is their INTERSECTION ("candidate_pairs" / "candidate_walls"). The Lipschitz screen is sharper at small R (it uses the exact gap at z-hat); the interval scan is sharper at large R (it sees the true geometry rather than a worst-case constant).
task4.candidate_table_method: lipschitz_screen: gap(z-hat) <= L * R with the constants above (necessary condition for contact, sound). interval_certified: the SAT gap / wall gap enclosed by mpmath.iv over the FULL box(z-hat, R) has lower bound <= 0, i.e. contact is not excluded on the box. The interval scan is dependency-pessimistic, so it is a SUPERSET of the true candidates and is also sound; the Lipschitz screen is the sharper of the two at small R. Wall combos are interval-scanned only for the 60 smallest gaps (the rest exceed 0.5 and cannot close at R <= 0.1 by the Lipschitz bound).

task5.force_balance_rule: For square i and coordinate c in {cx_i, cy_i, theta_i}: FJ stationarity gives sum_k lambda_k A[k,c] = 0 with lambda >= 0 (grad s = e_s touches only z[33], so this holds for BOTH the lambda_0 > 0 and lambda_0 = 0 branches). If all nonzero coefficients share a sign, those lambda_k are 0 and the rows are load-dead. Iterated to a fixed point. This SUBSUMES theory.md T1-b's corner-square rule (two orthogonal wall normals +x, +y).
not_proved: the sign test is evaluated at z-hat; the min |coefficient| that fires is recorded per firing so a neighbourhood statement can be made, but no interval extension over a region is done here (M3).
no torque/rotation propagation beyond the single-coordinate sign rule; no use of the magnitudes (a genuine static solve).

square-square edges are kept in BOTH axis graphs regardless of their normal direction (theory.md only removes orthogonal WALL edges). This is the conservative direction: it keeps more paths, so the reported cuts are valid but possibly not minimal.
gained (new) contacts are not in the graph; a stratum could reconnect a cut axis by acquiring a contact (Task 4 bounds which).
task5.per_k_note: frac_dead_by_loadpath = fraction of strata whose retained rows (after force-balance pruning) have NEITHER an x-wall-to-wall path NOR a y-wall-to-wall path. By T1-b those strata are FJ-free for lambda_0 > 0; the lambda_0 = 0 branch is empty at z-hat by Task 1b. "no_prune" repeats the count with the RAW L6 graph (theory.md T1-b as written, no force-balance refinement) so the two effects can be separated. frac_total_multiplier_collapse = the sign rule cascades until NO retained row can carry a multiplier: those strata are FJ-free outright, lambda_0 = 0 branch included, with no graph argument needed. All at z-hat gradients.

theory_md_cross_check.note: theory.md records x = 5, y = 3 ({22,23,25}), joint = 8 from the float recon. {22,23,25} IS a valid y-cut but it is not minimal: the MILP (and max-flow) minimum is smaller. The recon numbers appear to have cut the wall node directly rather than searching all cuts.

global_exhaustive.note: EXHAUSTIVE over all 2^38 - 1 nonempty break sets: only the 223 subsets of the 16 maximal Z(v) can be cone-alive, so the four tests can be applied to every break set in finite time. The listed survivors are the COMPLETE set of strata that need a real (V)/(C)/(F) certificate at the z-hat linearization with retained rows only.

order: 2. CONE-DEAD (T1-a): e_s not in cone{grad g_m, m in M}, exact from the vertex enumeration of Task 3 -- RETAINED rows only
3. TOTAL COLLAPSE (T1-b refined): the force-balance sign rule cascades to lambda = 0 on every retained row; kills lambda_0 = 0 too
4. LOAD-PATH (T1-b as written): no x- and no y-wall-to-wall path after pruning; kills lambda_0 > 0
survives_all: none of the four fires -- these need a real (V)/(C)/(F) certificate from M2/M3.
synthesis.caveat: tests 2-4 use the RETAINED rows at z-hat only; GAINED contacts (Task 4) can re-feed the cone and reconnect the load paths, and the gradients drift along the stratum. M3 must extend them over a region.
